name: Complete Recovery
desc:
Customer Service and Payment Specialist | $14.50 - $15.00/hr + Commission (~$2+/hr additional) | Phone Heavy, Equipment Recovery & Payment Collection 
Company: Complete Recovery Corp
Industry: Asset Recovery & Collections | Telecom, Medical, and Business Equipment
What Your Day Will Look Like:
Complete Recovery is an asset recovery company that works on behalf of cable, telecom, medical, and business equipment leasing companies. When a customer stops paying or a lease ends, your job is to reach out and either help them get caught up on payments or coordinate getting unused equipment back. Think modems, medical devices, security equipment, that kind of thing.
The company is genuinely upfront that they don't want scripted, robotic conversations here, they train employees to actually listen and use empathy rather than reading a memorized pitch. You'll be reaching people through calls, texts, emails, even postcards and letters, so this is a multi-channel outreach role, not just answering inbound calls. A lot of the job comes down to building enough trust with someone in a tough financial spot that they're willing to work with you rather than avoid you.
Because this touches on debt collection and payment recovery specifically, there's real regulatory structure behind how these conversations are supposed to go (state, federal, and company compliance rules), so accuracy and following procedure matters as much as the empathy piece.
assessment: Expect an assessment in pre-interview phase
wage: $14.50 to $15.00/hr base, plus commission (typically an extra $2.00 or more per hour based on account resolution performance).
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: Not stated in posting.
 Required Experience: 6 months contact center experience preferred. Previous customer service experience preferred, not strictly required.
 Preferred Experience: Prior collections or accounts receivable experience would likely translate well, though not stated directly.
 Required Skills:
Ability to build trust and communicate effectively with customers in a difficult financial situation
Comfort navigating multiple computer applications
High accuracy in account maintenance and documentation
Typing speed of at least 25 WPM
Logical problem-solving and multitasking
Strong oral and written communication
Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
Someone who is naturally empathetic but also comfortable having direct conversations about money and payment
Participants who don't mind a role that blends customer service with collections-style outreach
Anyone who values a genuine "never work a Sunday" schedule structure
People who can pass a federal background check
Someone motivated by commission on top of base pay, since resolving more accounts translates directly to more earnings
Not a Good Fit for:
Anyone who would struggle with a role centered on reaching out about overdue payments or equipment returns
Participants who cannot pass a federal background check, this is stated as a hard requirement
Someone who needs a fully fixed income without any performance-based variability
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
 Collections, payment recovery, customer service, account maintenance, asset recovery, accounts receivable, multi-channel outreach, negotiation, call documentation, compliance

Felony Friendly?: Not stated in posting or found in outside research. This role explicitly requires passing a Federal Background Check, which is a real, stated requirement, not something to assume flexibility around.
Drug Test: Yes, confirmed directly in the posting.
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
Application
Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you.
If assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen.
If phone screen passes you can expect the final interview.
 Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3-15 days on average.
Likely interview questions for this role:
Tell me about a time you had a difficult conversation with someone about money or payment and how you handled it with empathy.
How do you stay accurate and detail-oriented when managing account information?
Describe your approach to building trust with someone who might be avoiding a conversation with you.
How do you stay professional and compliant when following required scripts or disclosures in a collections-adjacent role?
other:
The company markets a no-script, empathy-based training approach, which is a genuine positive for someone who wants to actually problem-solve rather than recite lines, and aligns well with a participant who has said they enjoy this type of work
Career Pathway: Customer Service and Payment Specialist → Senior Payment Specialist → Team Lead → Collections Supervisor → Operations Manager
training: discussed in interview/ofer stage. must be available for any shift
